primary_claim: Applying gradient routing to an MNIST variational autoencoder (masking all latent dimensions except the one corresponding to the image's label during training) produces a 10-dimensional latent space that specializes one dimension per digit, enabling digit classification via argmax over the encoding at 92.58% accuracy despite no explicit classification loss.

effect.metric: digit classification accuracy via argmax over latent encoding

contradicts_or_qualifies: The Gradient Routing paper found extra regularization was often needed to split representations well, but here the default VAE regularization alone was sufficient
limitations_stated: Reconstruction quality is not very good
Uses the simplest possible architecture (MLP layers and ReLU)
Only a 10-dimensional latent space, which may constrain the representation
No data augmentation used, so it might not generalize well
Gradient routing targets an unnatural internal representation, which may cause the autoencoder to not fit the data as well
quote: we can classify digits to 92.58% accuracy by just taking the argmax over the encoding (which slider is the most positive), which I find pretty amazing.
